Just felt like sharing my own perspective on the matter. Since people clearly don't believe someone who is impaired in some way can't do wonderful things. Such a closed mindset.

I very much agree with this sentiment, like, how could anyone ever think disabilities make it impossible to create? I have really bad pelvic floor dysfunction. In the past, simply sitting down was perfectly fine to me. But over time. Sitting became painful, especially for long periods of time. It's progressed so badly that it becomes unbearable at around 1 hour of sitting. I need icepacks 24/7 just to manage the achiness I feel.

I'm also an artist like Paul. So when that started happening I was feeling awful. Since I grew up drawing digitally with a mouse. And then in my teens, got to switch to a drawing tablet that I cherished for many years. So when it felt like something I loved caused me physical strain, I was understandably upset.

But after months of having issues creating art because I just couldn't sit down to do it like I used to. I found a good drawing app on my phone and just kept at it. I longed to create art on my laptop like I did as a child for a while. But now I find it so freeing that I can just draw without causing too many flare ups. Cuz I can just lie down in a comfortable pose that doesn't involve sitting.

People are always so shocked when I say that I draw with my phone. But my app records progress in real time, so I always just show that as proof.

I doubt that my way of doing things and why is unique to me. Tho I am yet to find someone who creates similarly for a similar reason.

As always though, thank you so much, Paul. Your videos are always such a joy to enjoy when I'm having bad days with my disability.

There have been improvements with my condition, but nothing permanent as of yet. I'm just grateful to have found the means to keep creating despite my body trying to tell me no.

Ive been seeing what i personally think are very dumb arguments because people are very misinformed. AI 'art' is considered art because the result is prompted by a creative process by a human being. BUT it is extremely unethical because so many generators use copyrighted creative work (animations, illustrations, books etc) published online as data for these results. To make it more ethical is to have a system that limits this issue. E.g have a system that ensures that copyrighted creative works are not made available for these genrators to use. The problem is that the world wide web is such an open domain it i would be very difficult to regulate this, tho i am curious how different countries will approach this.

AI art does NOT make art more accessible, it is simply another method of making something look good just like other art media, because it gets direct information from data things that looks good/ cool/ beautiful/ inspiring etc (baisically what the human brain does but the brain is way more complex in how it hds information. Emotions/ info and memory processing/trauma etc affect this) and showing it to people, whatever thing that moves people from seeing things captured or developed by a human being.

Accessiblility in art actually means having art be available to people from different walks if life, including disability, socio-economic status etc etc, like designing an  ergonomic paint brushes for people with severe hand injury for example according to the individual artist's needs and goals in what art they make in what medium, and that includes the use of AI art (again considered very largely unethical), or a company making a range of budget versions of common art supplies like paint or alcahole markers etc or affordable digital art software like Krita and Blender.

You still need knowledge of art fundamentals in order to make good AI 'art', so no, it has very little to do with accessibility, knowing th fact that there are also people who want to physically make art, like painting, or physically making an art piece on a digital canvas. The way you could say AI art is accessable is that the AI art websites and software are user friendly because of the Ul (user interface) design, which in itself if an art form in a partial sense 😂 so now the user doesn't need to write the code to scrape from the internet or particular database and just type in a bunch of keywords into a promt box. Saying AI art is accessible is just an excuse for being too lazy to learn to make art in the professional context specifically, because those are the people affected. I don't care if you play with the art by yourself on an app, as long as the people using those apps know that if unregulated, you are using that work unethically if you distribute it for money. The acessibility argument undermines the weight of the issue with copyright

Speed doesn’t make the process unethical. If it’s okay for a human to learn a style and create something new, it shouldn’t suddenly be wrong when a machine does it in seconds. The issue isn’t the method. It’s that people are uncomfortable with how fast it’s happening and what it means for traditional business models. Yes, AI is taking jobs from real people, but so does any other technological advancement. You can either adapt or keep complaining, but AI is only going to improve over time. Personally, I would still commission a real artist because the work tends to look better. But if AI art improves to the point where there’s no real difference, I’d choose AI for cost and time efficiency.

And this is why we have art classes: so that we can learn to make art as we grow, and gain knowledge on drawing techniques, as well as make different forms of art, regardless if you can, or can’t do it.

Art is not as rewarding if you get it instantly. There’s no work, _or_ effort put into it. What makes human-made art special is the amount of heart, soul, and care put into it, with of course, work, and effort being the main keys to what makes art made by humans so special in the first place.


If cavemen were able to make cave drawing all those centuries ago, and even *inventing* art as a form of media without even having knowledge of what art is, then *anyone* can be an artist. All it takes is to do it on your own, especially with lots of practice so you can get better at it, and form creative ideas for what you want to make.
Hell, Pewdiepie challenged himself to draw every day for roughly 100 days, even though he’s not an artist to begin with. Within those long, laborious days, lasting a few months, he grew as an artist. He gotten better with his drawing strokes, he improved at drawing the anatomy of faces, he even looked at reference images to get an understanding of how the faces of the characters looked like before drawing them, _without_ tracing. ALL of that time goes by, and he improved on his drawing skills pretty quickly, almost as if he unlocked a hidden skill within him.


Ai could *never* come close to this by itself. The only thing that Ai is good for it being used as a _tool. _*_Not_* a *replacement.* That would be taking the lazy route to “becoming” an artist. This is not allowing you to grow into being one, because there’s no learning curve.
